The main conclusions are summarized as follows. $Ξ_c(2790)$ and $Ξ_c(2815)$ can be well explained as $Ξ_c1P\big|J^P=1/2^-,1\big\rangle_λ$ and $Ξ_c1P\big|J^P=3/2^-,1\big\rangle_λ$, respectively. $Ξ_c(2882)$ may correspond to $Ξ_c1P\big|J^P=1/2^-,0\big\rangle_ρ$ or $Ξ_c1P\big|J^P=1/2^-,1\big\rangle_ρ$; under this interpretation, $Ξ_cπ$ and $Ξ_c'π$ would be promising channels for its detection. $Ξ_c(2923)$ might be assigned to $Ξ_c'1P\big|J^P=3/2^-,1\big\rangle_λ$, but further confirmation is required. $Ξ_c(2939)$ is very likely to be $Ξ_c'1P\big|J^P=3/2^-,2\big\rangle_λ$ and has a good potential to be observed in the final states $Ξ_cπ$ and $Ξ_c'^{*}π$. $Ξ_c(2965)$ can be explained as $Ξ_c'1P\big|J^P=5/2^-,2\big\rangle_λ$ and $Ξ_cπ$ decay channel is a promising additional mode for future experimental searches. $Ξ_c(3055)$ and $Ξ_c(3080)$ can be assigned as the quark configurations $Ξ_c1D\big|J^P=3/2^+,2\big\rangle_{λλ}$ and $Ξ_c1D\big|J^P=5/2^+,2\big\rangle_{λλ}$, respectively. $Ξ_c(3123)$ is possibly state $Ξ_c'1D\big|J^P=1/2^+,1\big\rangle_{λλ}$ or $Ξ_c'1D\big|J^P=5/2^+,3\big\rangle_{λλ}$, with the latter being more favorable. Decay channels $Λ/ΣD$ are very likely to serve as a criterion for distinguishing between these two possible candidates.

title: A microscopic stochastic field theory for nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution based on a Doi--Peliti framework
abstract: We construct a reaction-based microscopic realisation of nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution in rapidity and impact-parameter space. Using the Doi--Peliti formalism, we derive the master equations, their operator representation, the exact hierarchy of factorial moments, and the coherent-state functional integral. The construction admits normalised complex configuration weights while retaining the algebraic conservation law of the gain--loss generator. Pomeron branching and merging yield the complex logistic equation \cite{Kohara:2026} under mean-field factorisation. Pomeron-catalysed odderon branching and ternary odderon fusion provide an odd sector whose evolution is driven by the pomeron background. Without transverse diffusion, the resulting equations admit an analytical solution in quadrature, allowing us to examine amplification, phase evolution, and nonlinear regulation. A specified matching between the first moments and the even and odd scattering profiles connects this evolution to elastic-scattering observables. Illustrative initial conditions produce a nonmonotonic forward ratio and a splitting between the $pp$ and $p\bar p$ channels, while the interference near a diffractive minimum remains sensitive to the relative phases and transverse profiles. These examples illustrate the effective dynamics without constituting a fit to data or a general proof of scattering unitarity.

title: Electromagnetic Structure of $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$ and $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons from a covariant three-body Faddeev equation
abstract: We investigate the electromagnetic structure of the ground-state $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$ and $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$ baryons using a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation within the rainbow--ladder truncation. We calculate the complete set of elastic spin-$3/2$ multipole form factors, $G_{E0}$, $G_{M1}$, $G_{E2}$, and $G_{M3}$. The leading electric and magnetic form factors become markedly harder from the charm to the bottom sector, revealing the substantially more compact electromagnetic structure of the $Ω_{bbb}^{-}$. For $Ω_{ccc}^{++}$, the electric form factor and charge radius at low momentum transfer agree well with the available lQCD results. From the magnetic-dipole form factor at zero momentum transfer, $G_{M1}(0)$, we obtain the magnetic moments $μ_{Ω_{ccc}^{++}}=1.26\,μ_N$ and $μ_{Ω_{bbb}^{-}}=-0.207\,μ_N$. For $G_{E2}$ and $G_{M3}$, the electric-quadrupole structure exhibits a stronger charm-to-bottom evolution than the charge-normalized magnetic-octupole structure. Finally, comparison of the charm and bottom systems shows that both $G_{M1}(0)$ and the relation between the electric and magnetic radii move closer to their leading nonrelativistic heavy-quark expectations as the quark mass increases.

title: Second-order evolution of spin shear tensor for massive spin-1/2 particles
abstract: We present the second-order evolution equation for the spin shear component of the spin tensor in spin-polarized fluids, using a classical description of the spin degrees of freedom. Employing a semi-classical kinetic theory for the massive spin-1/2 particles within the relaxation time approximation we obtain a relaxation-type equation describing the evolution of spin shear driven by various thermodynamic forces and high-order gradient corrections. This equation yields a new set of transport coefficients that govern the dynamics of the dissipative spin-shear tensor.

title: On-shell constituent approach to the light-front partonic energy-momentum tensor
abstract: The forward matrix elements of the energy-momentum tensor in momentum space, parameterized by gravitational transverse-momentum distributions (TMDs), provide a microscopic window into hadronic mechanical structure. While the longitudinal and transverse columns match to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, the light-front minus column involves the unintegrated parton energy $k^-$, leaving this sector undetermined in general quantum chromodynamics. Working within relativistic light-front constituent frameworks where active quarks are modeled as effective on-shell quasiparticles, we show that this energy factorizes algebraically. This establishes a closed matching relating all 32 gravitational TMDs to canonical vector TMDs up to twist-4, including target polarization and T-odd final-state interactions. This completion provides access to the light-front energy density and its transverse Sivers dipole distortion, demonstrates the local equivalence between convective energy and momentum transport velocities, and determines the longitudinal normal stress. Comparing longitudinal and transverse stresses yields a boost-invariant anisotropy ratio that charts the mechanical crossover from collinear confinement dominance to transverse isotropic balance. While formulated within the constituent approximation, these results offer baseline insights into the three-dimensional continuum mechanics of the nucleon.

title: Gravitational form factors of heavy quarkonia and their nonrelativistic expansion in a self-consistent light-front quark model
abstract: We investigate the gravitational form factors of the pseudoscalar heavy quarkonia $η_c(1S,2S)$ and $η_b(1S,2S)$ in a light-front quark model with physical radial wave functions represented by orthogonal mixtures of the two lowest harmonic-oscillator basis states $φ_{1S}$ and $φ_{2S}$. The Bakamjian--Thomas prescription is applied consistently to constituent matrix elements and Lorentz prefactors at the integrand level. Working in the $Δ^+=0$ frame with $Δ=P'-P$ and $t=Δ^2$, we extract $A_q(t)$ from the quark energy--momentum tensor components $T_q^{++}$, $T_q^{+i}$, and $T_q^{ij}$, and $D_q(t)$ from $T_q^{+-}$, $T_q^{-i}$, and $T_q^{ii}$ using appropriate momentum-transfer projections. The independent extractions agree in the full relativistic calculation and in the analytic nonrelativistic expansions through $ O(v^2)$, where $v=β/m_Q$, $β$ is the Gaussian width, and $m_Q$ is the constituent mass. At zero momentum transfer, the expansions give $D_q^{φ_{1S}}(0)=-v^2+ O(v^4)$ and $D_q^{φ_{2S}}(0)=-2/3-(13/3)v^2+O(v^4)$. The interference, defined as the sum of the two cross overlaps, first contributes as $D_q^{\mathrm{cross}}(0)=-(4/\sqrt{6})v^2+O(v^4)$. Thus, the pure Gaussian $1S$ contribution is suppressed, whereas a nonzero $2S$ admixture at fixed mixing angle leaves an $O(v^0)$ D-term in the physical ground state. Full numerical results for the mixed states illustrate the effects of heavy-quark flavor and radial structure on mass distributions and internal stresses.

title: Fisher-Rao Geometry of Gluon Saturation Fronts
abstract: How nonlinear gluon saturation erases the memory of initial conditions is a central question in high-energy QCD. We develop the Fisher-Rao information geometry of saturation fronts in the Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) equation and its Fisher-KPP diffusive limit. Using the normalized coordinate-space front density $p = \partial N/\partial\ln r^2$, we isolate the transverse metric $g^\perp_{θθ}$ that quantifies shape distinguishability once longitudinal propagation along the flow is factored out. Nonlinear saturation arrests diffusive broadening and freezes the Fisher speed. Transverse deformations exhibit a universal $t^{-4}$ relaxation in the Fisher-KPP asymptotic analysis, with full BK evolution providing numerical evidence for the corresponding $τ^{-4}$ behavior. We trace this steep power law to a relaxation mechanism: deforming the initial profile is equivalent, to leading order, to a spatial translation combined with an effective time delay of the universal relaxation flow. Extracting the translation and the delay from neighboring runs alone predicts the ratio of $g^\perp_{θθ}$ to its shift-control value within $1\%$ for Fisher-KPP and for BK up to $τ= 15$. For Fisher-KPP, the asymptotic front expansion yields the $t^{-4}$ law conditionally on stated analytic hypotheses, with a universal amplitude $C_*$ that agrees with numerical extrapolations to sub-percent accuracy. For BK, the asymptotic translation information exceeds its diffusive approximation by a factor of 3.5, which we attribute to the non-diffusive Levin-Tuchin saturation region. These results provide an information-geometric characterization of the approach to geometric scaling, consistent with the persistent sensitivity of pre-asymptotic HERA fits to initial shape parameters, and motivate systematic studies of parameter sensitivity in EIC kinematics.

title: The quantum magic of top quarks
abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

title: Heavy quark thermalization using phonon-heavy quark EFT
abstract: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles, due to large coupling strength and gluon occupation numbers. An alternative way to formulate a description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom is the interaction of the heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a natural occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we have derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Finally, we will use these coefficients to solve the Boltzmann equation for the heavy quark distribution, studying its thermalization in the QGP via soft phonon interactions.

title: Source shapes in coordinate and momentum space in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}$ = 200 GeV Au+Au collisions
abstract: In high-energy heavy-ion physics, femtoscopy aims to explore and understand the space-time characteristics of the collisions through investigating the correlation function of particle pairs. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown that the shape of the particle source function can be well described by the Lévy distribution, motivating further phenomenological studies. In this work, we perform a three-dimensional analysis of the source shapes for different particle-pair types in $\sqrt{s_\text{NN}}=200$ GeV Au+Au collisions generated with the EPOS event generator. In contrast to our previous analyses, where we fitted the one-dimensional projections of the pair distribution function, $D(ρ_j)$ ($j \in \{\text{out}, \text{side}, \text{long}\}$), now we reconstruct the three-dimensional $C(\boldsymbol{q})$ correlation function and fit it directly, as in experimental analyses. Furthermore, we now apply full three-dimensional fits instead of fitting the one-dimensional projections. We find that this approach results in smaller Lévy index values, while the direction averaged Lévy scale and the correlation strength remain largely unchanged, except for kaons. In the case of pions, the $α$ values are closer to the PHENIX data, showing a good agreement above 20\% centrality.

title: From High Energy Astrophysical Neutrinos to the Nobel : The History, Legacy and Science Behind the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics
abstract: This article briefly discusses the journey behind the discovery of the high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the making of the world's largest neutrino telescope that opened new portal to neutrino astronomy. It all started with the AMANDA experiment and how the strong conviction by Prof. Francis Halzen to transform a huge block of Antarctic ice into the largest and the most successful neutrino detector in the world and to work on it with relentless grit and determination to make it come true since Day 1 of the AMANDA project, led him to win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics. This is the story of some great scientists and engineers who dared to dream the impossible and made it happen through bold decisions, bold ideas, and innovative engineering heralding a new branch of astronomy. This leaves an enduring legacy of inspiration for future generations of aspiring scientists, who will look up to these scientific pioneers as role models and strive to follow in their footsteps.

title: Probing nuclear deformation through global $Λ$ polarization in U$+$U collisions at HIAF
abstract: We investigate the effects of nuclear deformation on global $Λ$ polarization in U+U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=2.85$~GeV using the JAM2 transport model, in view of future measurements at HIAF. The tip--tip and side--side configurations yield substantially larger global $Λ$ polarization than that in the body--body configuration. This separation grows with an increasing quadrupole deformation parameter $β_2$, highlighting the sensitivity of orientation-dependent polarization to nuclear deformation. These findings connect nuclear shape with hyperon spin, opening a new avenue for probing nuclear deformation through polarization measurements in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions.
